comparisons.evidence: Ta. paccavațam, paccatam a long piece of cloth used as a blanket, bedsheet, or screen. Ma. paccavațam an entire piece of cloth (32 cubits); blanket. Ko. paca'd (obl. paca't-), paca'd vara'ſ cloak sewed together from two lengths. Ka. paccavaļa, paccada a stout cotton cloth (24 cubits long and 2 cubits broad), used as a wrapper or cover at night. Kod. paccada white cloth for saris. Tu. paccade shawl. Te. paccadamu bed sheet, cloak. /Skt. pracchada a cover, wrapper, blanket. Pkt. pacchaa- garment, sheet. Cf. entry 241 for vațam, etc. < Skt. pața-.

comparisons.evidence: Ta. cantai a fair, market, Shandy, bazaar, multitude. Ma. canta a fair, weekly or annual market. Ko. caynt market. To. soty market day; week. Ka. sante, santi assemblage, fair or market, market-place. Kod. catte market. Tu. santé id., fair. Konda sata village market. Skt. samsthā- assembly (lex.; but cf. BHS samsthāgāra-, Pa. samthāgāraassembly hall); Pkt. *samthă-. Cf. also Skt. samsthāna- public place in a town, Pa. saņthāna- meeting place, market. The etymology usually given is Skt. samdhā-, which does not have the meaning 'assembly' (though samdhāna- does).
